newsitem.title: USA: Conrail in talks with Railroad Development.
newsitem.headline: Conrail in talks with Railroad Development.

text.p: Conrail Inc said on Monday it has chosen to negotiate exclusively with Railroad Development Corp of Pittsburgh to transfer ownership and freight operating rights of about 185 miles of rail lines in southern New Jersey.

Conrail had been analyzing three separate bids for the rights. While this transaction was subject to further due diligence, Conrail said it expected the deal to be completed before the end of the first quarter of this year.

Under the terms of the proposed transaction, Railroad Development would obtain rail freight routes serving corridors including Trenton-Bordentown, N.J., and Bordentown-Pennsauken-Camden, N.J., it said. The sale would also include part of Conrail's Pavonia Yard in Camden.

Conrail said it would continue to own and serve customers along the Penns Grove Secondary Line, between Woodbury, N.J. and Deepwater, N.J., and control dispatching of trains over other lines needed to reach the Penns Grove Secondary.
Terms of the proposed transaction would be subject to negotiation and Conrail board approval, it said.
